hints.content:
This is the process for determining the sine or cosine of any angle $\theta$:

1. Starting from the point $(1,0)$, move counterclockwise along the unit circle until the angle that is formed between your position, the origin, and the positive $x$-axis is equal to $\theta$.
2. The $x$-coordinate of that point is equal to $\cos(\theta)$ and the $y$-coordinate of that point is equal to $\sin(\theta)$.

According to this the definition, which angle corresponds to point $A$?

The angle that corresponds to point $A$ is $360\degree-30\degree=330\degree$.

[[☃ image 1]]

The $y$-coordinate of that point is $\sin(330\degree)$.

options.alt: A unit circle on an x y coordinate plane where the center of the unit circle is at the origin and the circumference of the circle touches (one, zero), (zero, one), (negative one, zero), and (zero, negative one). Point A is located at near four thirty thirty o'clock on the circle. A line segment extends from (one, zero) to point A. An angle from the arc starting at (negative one, zero) and opening clockwise to point A has an angle measurement of thirty degrees. The complete circumference around the circle has an angle measure of three hundred sixty degrees.

hints.content: In conclusion, the value of the $y$-coordinate of point $A$ is $\sin(330\degree)$.
